## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (75%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Reliability is 15%, Benign stays in the conformal set, and MUSK disagrees [F6].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 75%, Benign 25% | Normal favored, Benign plausible |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.15 / 8th percentile | Input suspect, image typical |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Disagrees on top class |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Normal | Neighbors all agree [F5] |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 1, 9, 11) · ↓ invasive · Strongest association with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Unreliable
- **Gland/tubule formation** (regions 2, 5, 6) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score; modest non-invasive association [F3] · Weak
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Mildly elevated; negligible contribution · Validated
- **Neoplastic nuclei** (regions 0, 3, 11) · context · Few counted; flagged insufficient for tumor-cell metrics · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect the classifier; normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Poor image quality or atypical staining (reliability 15%) distorts every probability shown here.
- A benign lesion is present, since Benign is in the set and MUSK disagrees.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 9, 11:** confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; this concept failed its spot check.
2. **Region 3:** look for infiltrating tumor in stroma; its score is mildly elevated.
3. **All regions:** check focus and stain quality behind the reliability flag.
